messages:
Maya Patel: FYI customer on Dedicated hit a burst during a live demo and saw lots of 429s. They say our SDK kept retrying and they ended up with duplicated create-ops (user records). They want repro steps and to know our SDK defaults.
Aj Chen: ugh. Which endpoint was it? mutating POSTs or streaming generation?
Maya Patel: POST /v1/deployments/rdw-gen/completions — high concurrency, no Idempotency-Key sent from their client. They used our JS SDK out-of-the-box.
Samir Rao: that explains duplicates. Our SDK by default retries non-fatal errors up to 3 times with exponential backoff + full jitter, and it retries on 429/5xx by default. If the app doesn't set an idempotency key for mutating requests, retries can cause duplicate side-effects.
Elena Gomez: Do we have the exact customer repro? logs?
Maya Patel: customer provided a small repro script and server logs. Repro gist: concurrency 30, request body creates a record, no idempotency header. They hit quota burst threshold and got a flurry of 429s.
Maya Patel: Repro script (customer):
```
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deployments/rdw-gen/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"create-user","email":"test+'$i'@example.com"}' &
done
wait
```
Samir Rao: ok good. Server response they attached looked like: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1715123500
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"burst quota exhausted for tenant"}
Aj Chen: So two issues: client-side no idempotency + SDK retries on 429s. Both combine to create duplicates.
Elena Gomez: What's our guidance to customers? change SDK defaults? or require Idempotency-Key?
Samir Rao: Guidance: always send an Idempotency-Key for mutating endpoints. SDK should enable idempotency helper for POSTs that create resources. For 429 specifically, follow Retry-After when present and use exponential backoff with jitter. We also recommend client-side token-bucket to shape bursts.
Maya Patel: Could we change SDK default to NOT retry 429 on mutating POSTs unless Idempotency-Key present? Customer is pushing for that to avoid accidental duplicates.
Samir Rao: We can. Backwards compat risk though. Alternative: SDK can add safe default: retries disabled for HTTP methods other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS unless idempotency key is provided. That keeps current behavior for reads but reduces duplicate mutations.
Aj Chen: That sounds reasonable. Can we show a config snippet customers can use now to opt-in?
Maya Patel: from SDK config:
```
// JS SDK example
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  retries: {
    maxAttempts: 0 // disable automatic retries for mutating requests
  },
  idempotency: {
    autoHeaderForMethods: ['POST','PUT','PATCH'] // opt-in to add Idempotency-Key when app allows
  }
});
```
Elena Gomez: also add a snippet for exponential backoff + jitter if they want custom retry logic:
```
function getBackoff(attempt){
  const base = 100; // ms
  const cap = 2000; // ms
  const exp = Math.min(cap, base * Math.pow(2, attempt));
  return Math.random() * exp; // full jitter
}
```
Maya Patel: Shared KB link for customers: SupportBot: <https://kb.redwood.ai/support/client-retries-idempotency> :pager:
SupportBot: Also note: if server returns Retry-After header, SDK respects it by pausing for that many seconds before retry. If Retry-After not present we use backoff heuristic.
BillingBot: Customer also opened a billing dispute claiming duplicate charges because a create triggered downstream paid actions. Please advise finance: attach list of request_ids and timestamps so we can audit.
Maya Patel: I pulled request_ids from their logs and sent to BillingBot.
Aj Chen: Ops question — can we surface a better per-tenant burst quota explanatory header, like X-RW-Burst-Remaining? That might help client-side throttlers.
Samir Rao: we already expose X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset. Adding more headers is possible but needs product signoff. For immediate mitigation: tell customers to implement a client-side leaky-bucket and idempotency keys.
Elena Gomez: For the support reply, let's: 1) Explain cause (429 + SDK retry semantics) 2) Provide quick mitigations (disable retries for mutating requests, add Idempotency-Key, implement client-side rate limiter) 3) Provide repro steps we used and patch suggestion for their SDK config 4) Offer dedicated call for migration help.
Maya Patel: Drafting message now and will include the exact config snippets and server log excerpts.
Aj Chen: One more edge: some customers want retries for short-lived 429 spikes. Could we offer a setting: "retryOn429Safe": true which only retries if request has Idempotency-Key and server 429 includes Retry-After <= 5s?
Samir Rao: yeah that is a solid feature. We'll add a request to roadmap.
Elena Gomez: closing loop — are we comfortable with public KB wording? Maya will post and close this thread when done.
Maya Patel: will post in an hour after legal ok. Thanks all :thumbsup:
SupportBot: Incident note created: INC-20240308-429-burst-sdk-retries (assigned to eng-runtime).
